summary: Review API boundaries for authorization, compatibility, idempotency, input/output contracts and failure semantics rather than endpoint style preferences.

must_inspect.why: Authentication alone does not prove permission for the specific resource or action.
false_positive_guards: Do not flag missing inline checks when authorization is enforced by a proven framework or upstream boundary.

must_inspect.why: Consumers depend on stable field, status, pagination and version semantics that can be broken without compiler feedback.
false_positive_guards: An intentional breaking version can be acceptable when versioning and migration are explicit.

must_inspect.why: Retries, webhooks and network ambiguity can duplicate side effects unless the contract defines replay behavior.
false_positive_guards: Read-only or naturally idempotent operations do not require synthetic idempotency machinery.
Do not infer runtime exposure solely from an unused route definition.
handoff_triggers: Live API behavior -> dedicated runtime/QA tooling
